P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes, with exchange-control conditions. Export proceeds normally must be brought in and 'liquidated' (converted to pesos) in the official FX market (MULC). For INDIVIDUALS (personas humanas), BCRA Com. 'A' 8330 (18 Sep 2025) removed the former USD 36,000/yr cap on the exemption for service exports. Com. 'A' 8417 (9 Apr 2026) extended the exemption from liquidation to all goods- and service-export collections of individuals, provided the funds are credited to a foreign-currency account in the exporter's own name at a local financial entity. The exemption does not apply to individuals acting for companies. Funds must still enter within the normal period (20 business days from collection per practitioners). Banks may not charge their own fees for crediting incoming foreign funds to individuals' accounts.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Individuals hold USD accounts at local banks, and under Com. 'A' 8417 export proceeds credited to the exporter's own local foreign-currency account need not be converted to pesos. Since Com. 'A' 8330, banks may not apply their own charges when crediting funds from abroad to such accounts (foreign intermediary costs may be passed on at cost).

sources.quote: Las entidades financieras no podrán aplicar cargos propios en operaciones que impliquen la acreditación de fondos del exterior en cuentas en moneda extranjera.

P3_local_gateways.question: Which local payment gateways can an individual or sole trader use to accept online payments?
P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for Argentina (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). Available: Paddle (not on its exclusion list; software sellers only, each seller reviewed); Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts); Polar (payouts); Whop (payouts); Dodo Payments (sellers); Etsy (seller payments via Payoneer); Google Play (developer registration); YouTube Partner Program. Not listed: Stripe (merchant sign-up).

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: An individual registers with ARCA (formerly AFIP), obtaining a CUIT (free; requires fiscal key level 3+ and a valid DNI), and enrols in a tax regime. The simplest is the Monotributo (Régimen Simplificado), which unifies IVA, income tax, pension contributions and health coverage into a single monthly payment, by category of annual gross billing (A to K). No company is required.

sources.title: Monotributista
sources.quote: El monotributo unifica el componente impositivo (IVA y Ganancias) y el componente previsional (aportes jubilatorios y obra social) en una única cuota mensual , haciendo más simple y ágil cumplir con tus obligaciones.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The CUIT (Clave Única de Identificación Tributaria), issued by ARCA. Residents with an Argentine DNI apply with fiscal key level 3 or higher and an image of their valid DNI (front and back), via the digital CUIT platform, the ARCA Móvil app or the 'Sistema Registral' service.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents (e.g. Argentine nationals living in Argentina, foreigners resident more than 12 months) are taxed on worldwide income with a foreign tax credit. Self-employed progressive rates run from 5% to 35% (FY2025: 35% above ARS 53,153,257). Monotributo replaces income tax and IVA with a fixed monthly fee by category. From 1 Aug 2026, category A (annual gross income up to ARS 12,009,410.45) pays ARS 49,527.18/month for services, and category K (up to ARS 126,610,838.75) pays ARS 1,614,446.04/month for services. Categories are updated twice a year.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: The general IVA rate is 21% (10.5% and 27% for specific items). Exports of goods and services are zero-rated, with input-VAT refund under art. 43 of the VAT Law. Monotributo taxpayers do not charge IVA separately, since the monotributo fee includes the IVA component (L1).

sources.quote: The VAT rate is 21%, although certain specific items are subject to a 27% or 10.5% rate.

sources.quote: VAT export reimbursement regime Exports of goods and services are treated as zero-rated transactions.

L4_vat_gst.notes: The VAT law's definition of exported services (use or effective exploitation abroad) was not read from the statute (infoleg 403).

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: Ley 25.326 (Personal Data Protection), supervised by the AAIP. Files and databases that allow obtaining information about people must be registered in the National Register of Personal Databases, done online via TAD with a fiscal key. The controller must register first, and registration does not expire. Files for exclusively personal use are exempt. When collecting data, controllers must inform data subjects of the purpose, recipients, the database's existence, and the controller's identity and address.

sources.title: Obligaciones de los responsables de bases de datos personales

sources.quote: Las bases de datos privadas destinadas a dar informes deben estar inscriptas en el Registro Nacional de Bases de Datos.

L5_data_protection.notes: Scope tension: AAIP pages use both 'bases ... que permitan obtener información sobre las personas' (broad) and 'destinadas a dar informes' (art. 21 wording). The guide should advise registering customer databases.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Ley 24.240 art. 34 and Civil and Commercial Code art. 1110: consumers in distance contracts may revoke acceptance within 10 calendar days from delivery or conclusion of the contract. Websites selling goods or services must include a 'botón de arrepentimiento' (repentance button), now governed by Disposición 954/2025, which repealed Res. 424/2020. The provider may not require prior registration or any extra step to use it.

sources.title: Disposición 954/2025 — Subsecretaría de Defensa del Consumidor

L6_consumer_ecommerce.notes: Disposición 3/2026 reportedly allows reasonable identity-verification steps; not captured.

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: (1) Monotributo: one fixed monthly payment covering IVA, income tax, pension and health, by billing category (L3). (2) FX liberalisation for individuals: export proceeds can stay in USD in a local account (Com. A 8417), with no own-bank fees on incoming transfers (A 8330). (3) Exports are zero-rated for IVA with refund (L4). The Knowledge Economy regime (Ley 27.506) was not researched for individuals.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (6) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. (7) Local official channel: Keep service-export proceeds in your own local USD account without converting to pesos (BCRA Com. 'A' 8417); banks may not charge their own fees on incoming transfers (P1/P2). Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
